target: Vi har inte setts på väldigt länge nu tyvärr.
english: We have not seen each other for a very long time unfortunately.
tip: The -s ending can mean each other: setts means seen one another, from se.

target: Min bror bor också i den här staden sedan förra året.
english: My brother has also lived in this city since last year.
tip: 'Sedan' (then/since) – dual meaning: 'sedan igår' (since yesterday), 'sedan gick vi' (then we left).

target: Huset är stort som vi såg i den gamla butiken igår.
english: The house is as big as the one we saw in the old shop yesterday.
tip: Swedish glues 'the' onto the noun as a suffix -et: huset = the house. There is no separate word for 'the'.

target: Det var den bästa filmen jag har sett på väldigt länge.
english: It was the best movie I have seen in a very long time.
tip: bästa is the irregular superlative of bra and god: den bästa filmen, the best film.

target: De har planterat blommor.
english: They have planted flowers.
tip: en-words ending in -a form plurals in -or: blomma becomes blommor.

target: Våga.
english: Dare.
tip: Verbs whose infinitive ends in -a keep that -a in the command form: våga = dare.

target: Slappna av.
english: Relax.
tip: Slappna av = relax. The particle av is stressed and stays right after the verb.

target: Försök igen.
english: Try again.
tip: Verbs with a consonant-final stem drop the infinitive -a in the command: försöka becomes försök = try.

target: Läs högt.
english: Read aloud.
tip: Add -t to an adjective to turn it into an adverb: hög becomes högt = aloud in läs högt.

target: Var modig.
english: Be brave.
tip: The command form of vara (to be) is var, not är: var modig = be brave.

target: Flytta stolen.
english: Move the chair.
tip: Swedish has no separate word for the; an en-word adds -en: stol becomes stolen = the chair.

target: Släck lampan.
english: Turn off the lamp.
tip: An en-word already ending in -a adds only -n for the: lampa becomes lampan = the lamp.

target: Dessutom regnar det.
english: Moreover, it's raining.
tip: A fronted sentence adverb forces verb-second: Dessutom regnar det puts regnar before det.

target: Vi parkerar i garaget.
english: We park in the garage.
tip: An ett-word adds -t for the: garage becomes garaget = the garage.

target: Bilen har blivit stulen.
english: The car has been stolen.
tip: Bli plus a past participle forms a passive: har blivit stulen = has been stolen.

target: Var snäll och hjälp mig.
english: Please be kind and help me.
tip: "Var snäll och" + imperative is a polite way to make a request.

target: Jag har fullständigt missat det.
english: I have completely missed it.
tip: In a main clause an adverb sits after the finite verb, before the main verb: har fullständigt missat = have completely missed.

target: Det här problemet måste vi lösa.
english: We must solve this problem.
tip: Fronting the object for emphasis pushes the subject after the verb: Det här problemet måste vi lösa.

target: Medan han jobbade lagade hon mat.
english: While he worked she cooked.
tip: When a clause with medan comes first, the main clause begins with its verb: lagade hon mat.

target: Jag förstår varför du är upprörd.
english: I understand why you're upset.
tip: After varför in a reported question there is no inversion: varför du är, never varför är du.

target: Jag ringer dig när jag kommer.
english: I'll call you when I arrive.
tip: Swedish uses the present tense for future actions: ringer and kommer here mean will call and will arrive.

target: Tystnaden efter stormen var nästan hörbar.
english: The silence after the storm was almost audible.
tip: The suffix -bar works like English -able: hörbar = audible, from höra plus -bar.

target: Eftersom det var sent gick vi hem.
english: Since it was late we went home.
tip: Eftersom means because and opens a reason clause: eftersom det var sent = because it was late.

target: Restaurangen som ligger på hörnet är ny.
english: The restaurant on the corner is new.
tip: Som is the all-purpose relative word for who, which or that: restaurangen som ligger = the restaurant that is located.

target: Jag frågar om hon vill följa med.
english: I ask if she wants to come along.
tip: Om means whether in a reported yes/no question: frågar om hon vill = ask whether she wants to.

target: Filmen som vi såg igår var bra.
english: The movie that we saw yesterday was good.
tip: When som is the object of its clause you may drop it: Filmen (som) vi såg = the film we saw.

target: Vännen som jag träffade igår mår bra.
english: The friend I met yesterday is doing well.
tip: To feel well uses the verb må, not känna: han mår bra = he is doing well.

target: Vi hoppas att vädret blir bra verkligen.
english: We really hope the weather will be nice.
tip: Hoppas ends in -s so it looks passive, but it is active and means 'we hope': vi hoppas att.

target: Jag berättade för honom att vi inte kunde.
english: I told him that we couldn't.
tip: Berätta needs för before the listener: berättade för honom = told him.

target: Hon är säker på att hon har rätt.
english: She is sure that she is right.
tip: Ha rätt, literally to have right, means to be right: hon har rätt = she is right.
